qt: to the Commission Elena Yoncheva (ECR) Subject:

Honey labels identify the responsible food business operator, who may be a retailer or brand owner, while lot codes need not publicly identify the actual final packing establishment. A separate lot indication may also be omitted under Article 5 of Directive 2011/91/EU1. Article 4a(1)(e) of Directive 2001/110/EC2 provides for Union-wide honey traceability requirements. The related feasibility work must assess digital solutions, including, where appropriate, a unique identifier. 1.
What is the timetable and current scope of this feasibility work, and will it assess a human-readable identifier of the actual packing site linked to a free public establishment register?

Does the Commission consider that the existing delegation permits mandatory public identification on retail packs and publication of establishment data, including safeguards for natural persons; if not, will it propose the necessary amendment to the basic legislation?

How will it ensure unambiguous links between retail packs, batches and packing sites, including private labels, contract packing, imported retail packs and date-based lot exemptions, while reusing existing registers and minimising the burden on small beekeepers?

Directive 2011/91/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 December 2011 on indications or marks identifying the lot to which a foodstuff belongs (OJ L 334, 16.12.2011, p. 1, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2011/91/oj). 2 Council Directive 2001/110/EC of 20 December 2001 relating to honey (OJ L 10, 12.1.2002, p. 47, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2001/110/oj). 1
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (24.11.2026) Directive 2001/110/EC1 provides that the Commission is to carry out a feasibility study before adopting a delegated act setting Union-wide traceability requirements for honey by 14 June 2029. The Directive2 provides for the feasibility study to include an analysis of available digital solutions or methods, including, where appropriate, a unique identifier code or similar techniques. Nothing more specific can be said at this stage. The feasibility study will assess available options, fully taking into account proportionality and the objective of minimising administrative burden.
